old/vista-gate.2026-10-16.webp.prompt:
A painted vista for the landing screen of a space trading game: futuristic, painterly, a cinematic matte painting with visible brushwork, wide 16:9. No text, lettering, logos, UI, borders or frames.

Prism art direction: slightly retro corporate futurism, like a 1970s or 1980s corporate brochure or airbrushed space art: smooth white curves, chrome trim and tinted glass, soft gradient skies, gentle pastel accent lights, a polished optimistic sheen that feels a little dated and a little too perfect.

Art bible for the Quire system. Palette: rust brown, dark grey, off-white, charcoal and pale sky blue. Lighting: Hard white starlight on bare rock with no atmosphere to soften it: long black shadows, blown highlights on cream ridges, a black sky even at midday. Indoors, even, shadowless, slightly cool light with no visible source, and a faint glow from the foundry vents. Architecture: Seamless white towers and low glassy halls on the day side, with no visible joins, doors or signs until you are standing at them. Night-side domes are clean and pale, ribbed with white struts. Stations are smooth lattices of white and glass, and security craft are gloss black. Materials: White ceramic panel, poured glass, brushed alloy, black polymer. Dust coats everything outdoors in rust and ash, and every indoor surface has been wiped within the last few minutes. Mood: Calm, clean and watched. Everything is orderly, polite and slightly too quiet, and the unease is under the surface and never shown. Design language: Prism's language: sleek, seamless, white and glass, with luxury that never looks lived in. Staff wear pale fitted uniforms with a single clean seam of colour, and security wears gloss black. Nothing visibly worn is allowed to stay visible.

The place: Quire Gate, the relay station of the system, a relay array in open space between the worlds. A working settlement of a few million. The light comes from a white star.

The scene: A white lattice of the relay array fills the foreground, with glass panels and folded dishes catching hard white starlight. Gloss-black security cutters sit against its pale frame. Below, Quire hangs rust brown against the black, wrapped in a thin glittering haze of debris. Further out a loose scatter of rock, the Assay, glints in blue and silver, and the tan and rust bands of Tamsin lie beyond.

Composition: keep the left two fifths of the image darker and calmer, with no focal point there, because the port's text panel is drawn over it; the main interest sits right of centre.

The attached image is the style reference for this faction's systems, from another of them, for the painting only: match its brushwork, finish and treatment of light, within this faction's art direction above. Take nothing else from it: not its landscape, sea, cliffs, buildings, rings or layout. The ground, sky and colours come from the description above.

Quire is a rust brown world of bare rock and dust with no water and no plants: dark ashen grey plains and crater floors, rust brown higher ground, cream ridges and crater rims, under a black sky; a glittering haze of orbital debris rings it. The light comes from a white star.

The scene: A flat ashen landing apron under a black sky, hard white sunlight throwing long black shadows. Beyond it stand tall white foundry towers, seamless and glass-faced, with heat shimmering above their vents. Rust-brown ridges and cream crater rims rise behind them. High overhead a glittering haze of debris arcs across the sky like a broken ring. A single armoured core carrier waits near the edge of the apron, ringed by gloss-black escort craft.
